facts.text: Browns Point was originally called Point Harris after sailmaker Alvin Harris of the Wilkes Expedition, but residents renamed it for an early landowner.
The Browns Point Lighthouse, first lit on December 12, 1887, was once fully staffed but is now fully automated.
The local Browns Point Improvement Club owns much of the land beside the lighthouse and is famous for its annual Browns Point Salmon Bake.
The Salmon Bake began in the 1940s, founded by pioneer Jerry Meeker, and is held every even‑numbered year during the first weekend of August.
Browns Point’s community is served by Browns Point Elementary, Meeker Middle, and Stadium High School.
The Points Northeast Historical Society preserves the area’s heritage and hosts events such as the 1986 Seattle Times feature on the lighthouse’s history.
